dish: Kanto-daki (Osaka oden), saezuri whale-tongue oden and sweet-simmered octopus
w: Founded in 1844 and billed as Japan's oldest oden restaurant, now run by the fifth generation; the counter serves kanto-daki oden, the signature saezuri (whale tongue) and sweet-simmered octopus, and was a haunt of writers Oda Sakunosuke and Kaikō Takeshi (Time Out Osaka; GLT/JTB Publishing).

Old-school Sennichimae okonomiyaki house cooking to order; its signboard dish is the suji negiyaki, beef strips and negi in a fluffy batter. Named by Time Out Osaka and Inside Osaka among Namba's okonomiyaki standbys and profiled by Savor Japan.

Dōtonbori okonomiyaki institution run across three generations, with a near-permanent queue; known for its yamaimo-yaki made with a mountain-yam batter (including a vegetarian, gluten-free version) (Inside Osaka; GLT/JTB Publishing).

Near-seventy-year-old okonomiyaki specialist by the Dōtonbori arcade, known for a cabbage-heavy, light batter; order the Ajinoya Mix (pork, squid, octopus, shrimp) or the negiyaki (Inside Osaka; GLT/JTB Publishing).

dish: Kushikatsu with a house sauce simmered over four days
n: Kushinobo Hozenji Honten (串の坊 法善寺本店)
address: Hōzenji area, Namba, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan
w: Kushikatsu house opened in 1950 by Hōzen-ji, behind a red noren; skewers come with a sauce stewed for over four days from vegetables, chicken bones, sea-bream heads and shrimp (japan-guide Osaka Food Guide; Savor Japan).
